title: Make an exhaustive list of incompatibilties with SGML
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Dear all,

For some while now, I'm writing my own SGML parser in Java (and in the future possibly in other languages), because I see that most implementations aren't fully compliant, over two decades old and/or not understable or usable in other projects I want to build. The goal is to read ISO 8879, write a fully compliant library and publish it in one or more languages for others to use.

One of those projects could be a simple HTML page viewer. Just HTML to start with. No CSS or JavaScript for the moment. Or a webcrawler, or a whole browser or browser engine. You name it. However, there are some problems with this.

HTML 1 (TBL), HTML 2, HTML 3 and HTML 4 are applications of SGML. The HTML parsers of these versions could be in fact just SGML parsers. Not able to parse some correct HTML would be an error in the SGML parsing implementation, because HTML rules where SGML rules. I'm aware this was the case with comment parsing, where browsers mostly failed to parse comments the SGML way.

HTML 5 is different. It is said it isn't an application of SGML anymore. However, I haven't seen much argumentation for why that is the case. Some people said it was because `<!DOCTYPE html>`, with the missing SGML literals, but production 110 of ISO 8879 allows those missing literals, so that ain't it. There may be some other claims that aren't simply true. The only reason I found is that comment issue I mentioned above (@Hixie). Sure, that will cause a problem with my SGML parser, but I can think about solutions to allow custom handling for that.

That is why I created this issue. I would like to see a list of incompatibilities between HTML 5 and SGML, including some arguments why this happened to be so. In case of the comments bug, it was likely because browsers and/or website builders failed to understand SGML comments, implemented those wrong already in early versions of HTML, with HTML 5 later embracing this bug as feature, because it existed for so long and would break existing technology. However, I think the list is longer than just this comment thing, but I'm just not aware of any other problems now.

Possibly we could make some appendix with this list. For me, and maybe for others too, it would make it very easy to write a SGML parser that also understands HTML 5.

Thanks in advance

Ben
